introduction: This level introduces Gauss's Law for analyzing complex symmetrical charge distributions, the behavior of electric dipoles, and the fundamental mechanics of capacitors.

core_concepts.title: Electric Flux ($\Phi$)
core_concepts.description: The total number of electric field lines passing perpendicularly through a given surface area. $\Phi = \vec{E} \cdot \vec{A} = EA \cos\theta$.

core_concepts.title: Gauss's Law
core_concepts.description: The net electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface is equal to $1/\epsilon_0$ times the net charge enclosed by the surface: $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\epsilon_0}$.

core_concepts.title: Electric Dipole
core_concepts.description: A system of two equal and opposite charges ($+q, -q$) separated by a small distance ($2a$). The dipole moment is $p = q \times 2a$, directed strictly from the negative to the positive charge.

core_concepts.title: Capacitance ($C$)
core_concepts.description: The ability of a system to store electric charge: $C = Q/V$. For an ideal Parallel Plate Capacitor with vacuum between plates: $C = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

important_entities.name: Dielectric Constant ($K$)
important_entities.significance: When a dielectric material is fully inserted between the plates of a capacitor, the capacitance increases by a factor of $K$: $C' = K \cdot C$.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Source of E in Gauss's Law
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In the formula $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = \frac{q_{\text{in}}}{\epsilon_0}$, the flux depends ONLY on the enclosed charge ($q_{\text{in}}$). However, the Electric Field ($\vec{E}$) on the left side of the equation is the net field due to ALL charges, both inside and outside the surface.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For the same distance $r$ (where $r \gg a$), the electric field on the axial line of a dipole is exactly twice the magnitude of the electric field on the equatorial line: $E_{\text{axial}} = 2 E_{\text{equatorial}}$.

exam_strategy_tips: Capacitor combination formulas are the exact mathematical opposite of Resistor formulas. In series: $1/C_{\text{eq}} = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2$. In parallel: $C_{\text{eq}} = C_1 + C_2$.
